newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at 35.88/89 in high volume trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at 35.88/89 in high volume trade.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.88/89 to a dollar on Monday compared with the opening quote of 35.89/91, dealers said.
They said the market was steady but saw high volumes.
The day opened at weekend levels and the rupee soon stabilised at 35.87/88 to a dollar.
"Some banks were long (on dollars) and this induced some selling in the morning," said a dealer at a state-run bank. He said the rupee saw a day's high of 35.87 and a high of 35.8950.
"The dollar failed again to surpass the 35.95 barrier as lacklustre demand met with adequate supply pushing it to 35.89 at close," a European bank said in its forex commentary.
"The significance of 35.95 is that on January 30 last year, the rupee fell through this barrier for a historic slide to 38.5 on February 6," it said.
The dollar's retreat from the 35.90-plus level indicated consolidation in the 35.85-35.95 range before an eventual breakout, it said.

"With inflation rising to a 56-week high of 7.58 percent and the Congress Party putting United Front government on a watch list, the run up to budget in February may turn out to be eventful," it said.
The treasurer at a German bank in Bombay said he did not expect the rupee to breach the 36 per dollar barrier until mid-February.

He said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) would not want the rupee to depreciate at this stage because of its implications for the redemption of over $2.0 billion in India Development Bonds before March.
Premia opened lower in the forward dollar market on Monday but institutional buying pushed up the premia by about five paise, dealers said.

"I also heard the RBI was receiving (premia against forward dollar) in a passive way, but can't confirm this," said another dealer. The RBI was keen on low premia to ensure that Indian banks continue to draw expatriate Indian dollar accounts, he said.
